roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Mukilteo, WA?
roles.costP1: Tile in Mukilteo prices out at roughly $14–$26 per square foot installed — tile, thinset and setting materials, substrate prep and the labor combined, with labor from $11/sq ft on its own. Tub-shower surrounds go $3,200–$6,800, a roughly 45 sq ft bathroom floor goes $900–$1,600, and a full bathroom — floor, shower, niche — usually finishes at $6,500–$14,000.
roles.costP2: Here's what catches people: the install cost tracks the tile's format, not its price. A modest $4 mosaic can cost more on the labor line than a $12 slab-look porcelain plank — every extra cut and every extra grout joint is time, and time is the bill.
roles.costNote: Mukilteo ranges, current to August 2026 — tile plus materials plus labor. Treat the written quote from your free estimate as the real number.
roles.layersLead: The stack runs seven layers deep, in strict order. Open a failed shower near the water and one is missing — the membrane, nearly every time — dropped for a few-hundred-dollar saving and repaid a hundredfold.
roles.whyP1: By the time a shower leak shows itself, it's old news. Moisture slides past grout, saturates the substrate, and reappears seasons later as a soft spot down the hall or a bloom on the ceiling underneath. The fix by then involves framing, subfloor, drywall and starting the tile from zero.
roles.whyP2: Waterproofing is roughly one-tenth of a shower's cost. Striking that line item remains the priciest deletion in home remodeling.
roles.scopeH2: Tile work we take on in Mukilteo
roles.scopeIntro: Prices below are floors, not ceilings — format, substrate condition and layout all move them. The binding number is written at your house, free.
roles.cardShower: Assembly in strict order: pre-slope, bonded membrane, documented flood test, then curbed or curbless entry, niche and tile. The invisible half of the job is the half that matters.
roles.cardFloors: Kitchens, baths, entries, laundry and mudrooms. We flatten the subfloor first and add an uncoupling layer wherever radiant heat or seasonal movement demands one — vital where condensation lingers.
roles.cardBacksplash: Subway, herringbone, slab-look porcelain or mosaic sheet. Outlets cut precisely, edges trimmed out, and a grout color picked for your counter instead of the factory-default white.
roles.cardHeated: An electric mat over an uncoupling membrane, resistance-verified twice — before setting and after — on a dedicated circuit. The window is while the floor's open; afterward the math never works.
roles.cardRepair: Chalky grout, hairline cracks, corners pulling loose in the shower. We say plainly whether a surface fix will hold or the substrate beneath is finished.
roles.cardDemo: Tile, thinset and backer board out under plastic sheeting and negative air, hauled the same day. Nothing staged in the driveway, nothing left for you to dump.

roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Mukilteo, WA?
roles.faqA1: In Mukilteo, installed tile runs about $14 to $26 per square foot with tile, setting materials, prep of the substrate and labor all in — the labor line starts at $11 per square foot by itself. Surrounds for a standard tub-shower price at $3,200 to $6,800; a complete bathroom — floor, shower, niche — usually totals $6,500 to $14,000. What drives cost is format rather than price per box: mosaics and large-format both demand far more labor per foot than a standard 12×12.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Mukilteo?
roles.faqA2: For a standard alcove shower, Mukilteo owners should budget $3,200 at the low end and $6,800 at the top — demolition, bonded waterproofing, a pre-sloped pan or base, setting, niche and grout all inside. Curbless entries, benches, steam and floor-to-ceiling stone climb beyond that. Waterproofing claims barely a tenth of the total, yet it's what heads off the five-figure rebuild.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: No exceptions, ever. Behind each shower goes a bonded assembly: pre-sloped base first, then an ANSI A118.10 membrane, liquid or sheet, taken wall-high, with every corner, seam and penetration sealed. Before a single tile is placed we flood the pan for 24 hours and photograph the result for your records. Salt-air houses should hear this twice: grout and tile only shed water, and the membrane underneath is the sole layer that truly stops it.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: A Mukilteo bathroom typically wraps in four to six working days. Demo with dust containment opens the schedule; substrate repair and waterproofing follow, capped by 24 hours of flood testing; tile setting fills the next day or two; grout, silicone and trim wrap the schedule. The shower then waits one more day — 24 hours of grout cure — before water touches it. Floors alone usually finish inside two days.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Porcelain wins anywhere water or traffic is involved — under 0.5% absorption, a denser body, better chip resistance. Ceramic is the economical, perfectly good answer for walls and backsplashes. Our Mukilteo spec is simple: porcelain on every floor and every shower floor, with ceramic and glass reserved for the vertical surfaces where they shine.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes. For $11 to $16 per square foot, installed and including the thermostat, an electric radiant mat goes under the tile — over an uncoupling membrane, resistance-tested twice and wired to its own circuit. Gray mornings on the bluff make it feel less like luxury and more like sense, but the timing is fixed: it's only worth installing while the floor is already up.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Usually, yes. Tear-out with haul-away starts around $3.50 per square foot and buys you the one thing you can't get otherwise: a clear view of the subfloor for rot, movement and height at the doorways. Setting new tile over old is occasionally fine on a flat, sound and firmly bonded surface, but it lifts the finished floor and hides exactly the problems demolition would have exposed.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Mukilteo?
roles.faqA8: Backsplashes in Mukilteo kitchens run $1,100 to $2,200 installed for a typical 30 square foot layout — outlets cut in, edges trimmed, grout chosen against the counter. Expect the upper end for mosaic sheets, herringbone, a picture-framed panel behind the range, or slab-look porcelain: layout and cutting time is what you're paying for.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Often. Starting at $8 per square foot, repair and regrout covers stained or crumbling grout, isolated impact cracks, and shower corners where old grout should come out in favor of silicone. The line we draw: hollow-sounding tiles, tiles loosening in a spreading pattern, or a soft wall mean the substrate has failed, and a cosmetic fix would only postpone the inevitable. We identify which case is yours before quoting.
roles.faqQ10: Which Mukilteo neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: Every part of Mukilteo — Old Town by the ferry, Harbour Pointe, Chennault Beach, Olympus Terrace, Japanese Gulch, the Paine Field side, Lake Serene, Picnic Point, Meadowdale and Mariner — plus Everett, Edmonds, Lynnwood, Mill Creek and, when the job calls for the boat, Clinton across the water.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: Every tile job leaves with a 2-year workmanship warranty — twice the length of our carpet coverage, since tile failures like to wait a year or two rather than a week or two. Choose a manufacturer's complete bonded system and that maker's warranty rides along too. We photograph both the membrane and the passed flood test, so when the house eventually lists, the evidence is sitting in a folder.
